title: Shadowfax to acquire WeFast India assets, Borzo IP for Rs 23.3 Cr
summary:
Shadowfax Technologies has agreed to acquire select business assets of WeFast India and technology and intellectual property (IP) rights associated with Borzo for $2.5 million (approximately Rs 23.3 crore) as the logistics company expands into on-demand intra-city goods transportation.
The transaction involves two separate agreements. Shadowfax will acquire technology, software and related IP rights in India from Incrin Limited for $2 million, along with a licence for the BORZO trademark for $50,000.
Under a separate agreement, Shadowfax will purchase identified business assets of Wefast India Private Limited for $450,000 in Indian rupees. These include contracts, equipment, domain names, databases and related technology. The agreement also provides for the transfer of identified employees.
The transactions are subject to customary conditions precedent and are expected to be completed by March 31, 2027.
The deal will allow Shadowfax to extend its logistics services to small and medium businesses (SMEs) and customer-to-customer (C2C) deliveries, according to a press release.
Founded in Mumbai in 2016, WeFast operates across more than five cities. The company has over 32,000 delivery partners who complete more than 1.2 crore deliveries annually. It generated around Rs 200 crore in adjusted revenue in CY2025.
The transaction will give Shadowfax access to WeFast's existing network and customer base in the intra-city logistics segment. The company plans to combine its technology and delivery network with WeFast's operations to serve shop owners, distributors and individual users.
Shadowfax said the deal builds on its existing hyperlocal delivery business. The company has over 3.8 lakh delivery partners across more than 16,000 pin codes.
In FY26, Shadowfax launched Shadowfax 360, an express parcel network for SMEs and D2C brands. The platform crossed 6,700 transacting sellers within two quarters of its launch.
Shadowfax's hyperlocal business reported 87.7% year-on-year revenue growth to Rs 341 crore in Q2 FY27.
Shadowfax co-founder and CEO Abhishek Bansal said the acquisition will help the company expand its logistics platform across express parcels, hyperlocal fulfilment and on-demand goods transportation.
In August 2021, WeFast rebranded as Borzo to bring its operations across 10 countries under a single brand. As part of its expansion plans, the company raised $35 million in a Series C funding round led by Mubadala, with participation from VNV Global, Russian Direct Investment Fund (RDIF) and Flashpoint Venture Capital, among others.

title: GST department conducts search at Turtlemint subsidiary in Mumbai
summary:
The Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax (GST) Department has initiated inspection, search and seizure proceedings at the premises of Turtlemint Insurance Broking Services, a wholly owned subsidiary of insurance distribution platform Turtlemint.
In a regulatory filing on November 24, Turtlemint Fintech Solutions said GST officials initiated the proceedings under Section 67 of the Maharashtra GST Act, 2017, on November 23.
The search was conducted at the subsidiary's registered office at The ORB Sahar, Marol Village, Andheri East, Mumbai.
The company said its subsidiary is extending full cooperation to the authorities and providing the required information, documents and clarifications in connection with the proceedings. It also said it will keep the stock exchanges informed about further developments, if any.
Turtlemint added that the regular business operations of both the company and its subsidiary remain unaffected. It also reiterated its commitment to conducting business in compliance with applicable laws and regulations.
This is not the first time Turtlemint has faced GST-related proceedings. The company had earlier received penalty orders aggregating to Rs 51.2 crore for the period between FY18 and FY23.
The penalties followed show-cause notices issued by the Directorate General of GST Intelligence (DGGI), which alleged that Turtlemint had raised invoices on insurance companies without the actual supply of services. The company challenged these orders before the GST Appellate Authorities.
Founded in 2015 by Dhirendra Mahyavanshi and Anand Prabhudesai, Turtlemint operates an insurance distribution platform that enables insurance agents and advisors to sell policies across categories, including life, health and motor insurance.
The company competes with Policybazaar and InsuranceDekho in India's digital insurance distribution market.

title: Lawvek raises $550K in pre-seed round led by Neon Fund
summary:
AI-powered vendor recovery platform Lawvek has raised $550K in a pre-seed funding round led by Neon Fund, with participation from Inzas Ventures.
The fresh capital will be used to expand its enterprise customer base and strengthen its platform’s ability to identify and recover money owed to businesses by their vendors, Lawvek said in a press release.
Co-founded this year by Amrit Khandelwal and Sudip Chhatui, Lawvek helps enterprises recover vendor overcharges, missed rebates and service credits. It uses AI agents to reconcile contractual terms with invoices, usage data and service records.
The problem stems from enterprises having pricing agreements, discounts and service commitments spread across contracts, billing records and operational data. This makes it difficult to track whether vendors have fulfilled their obligations.
According to McKinsey, unmet supplier commitments can cost large enterprises roughly 2% of their spending. For a company with $1 billion in annual expenditure, this could translate into approximately $20 million in annual losses.
Lawvek’s platform analyses vendor contracts against billing, usage and service records to identify discrepancies. These include price hikes beyond agreed caps, volume discounts missing from invoices and prepaid capacity that businesses may not fully utilise.
When the platform identifies money owed through rebates or service credits, it calculates the amount, collects supporting evidence and submits claims on behalf of customers. It also follows up with vendors and verifies whether the recovery has been reflected in invoices or received as a refund.
The startup is currently helping enterprises in the US identify instances of vendor overpayments and cases where they receive less than what was agreed in their contracts.

title: CortexSpark Ventures enters India’s VC market with SEBI approval for Rs 1,000 Cr deep-tech fund
summary:
CortexSpark Ventures has entered India’s venture capital ecosystem with the launch of Viksit Bharat Fund-I, a Rs 1,000 crore deep-tech fund, following registration with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI). Registered as CortexSpark Ventures Alpha Fund, the fund is a Category II Alternative Investment Fund (AIF) with an additional greenshoe option of Rs 400 crore.
The fund will invest across six sectors: space tech, defence tech, embodied AI and robotics, enterprise AI, medtech and bio-AI, and energy and advanced materials. Led by managing partners Vinay Peshwa and Sanjay Khanduri, the firm plans to back startups developing proprietary technologies and addressing complex technological challenges.
CortexSpark Ventures plans to combine AI-enabled investment processes with scientific expertise, human judgement and global networks. The firm describes its approach as “The venture fund for AI, by AI.”
The fund's investment thesis focuses on startups with defensible intellectual property, strong technical foundations, experienced founders and clear commercialisation pathways. Its entry comes amid growing investor interest in research-intensive sectors such as space, defence, robotics and advanced technologies.
The fund's Investment Committee will be chaired by Manoj Kohli, global business advisor and former country head of SoftBank Group. Kohli was also the former CEO and MD of Bharti Airtel.
Its advisory committee includes N. Vedachalam, former director of ISRO’s Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre, who contributed to India's cryogenic propulsion programme and several space missions, and Ashutosh Sharma, former secretary of the Department of Science and Technology and Institute Chair Professor at IIT Kanpur.
The firm is also developing CortexSpark OS, an AI-enabled fund management platform to support deal sourcing, screening, due diligence and portfolio monitoring. It also plans to assist portfolio companies with product commercialisation, hiring, business development, access to institutional and enterprise customers, and connections with international markets and follow-on investors.
Through Viksit Bharat Fund-I, CortexSpark Ventures aims to back Indian startups developing proprietary technologies for strategic industries and global markets, with a focus on taking research-led innovations towards commercialisation.

title: Swish spends Rs 145 Cr to generate Rs 48 Cr revenue in FY26
summary:
India’s 10-minute food delivery segment has attracted players such as Swish, Zomato, Swiggy, Zepto and Rebel Foods, as companies experiment with freshly prepared meals delivered within minutes. However, the category has seen several setbacks, with Swiggy shutting down Snacc, Zomato pausing Quick, Rebel Foods closing Quickie within a year of launch and Zepto scaling back its Zepto Cafe amid weak demand.
Swish is building its business in this emerging category through an ultra-fast food delivery model and currently operates across five cities. The startup is nearing Rs 50 crore in annual revenue, but its expansion has come with high operating costs, particularly employee expenses, pushing its losses up nearly 5X to Rs 91 crore in FY26.
The Bengaluru-based startup recorded an 11.9X jump in revenue from operations to Rs 47.6 crore in the financial year ended March 2026, according to its financial statements reviewed by Entrackr.

Founded in 2024 by Aniket Shah, Ujjwal Sukheja and Saran S., Swish operates a network of neighbourhood cloud kitchens that prepare and deliver fresh meals within 10 minutes. The startup currently has a presence across five cities: Bengaluru, Gurugram, Noida, Delhi and Ghaziabad.
Sale of food products was the company's sole source of operating revenue. It also earned around Rs 6 crore in interest income on bank deposits, taking its total income to Rs 53.75 crore during FY26.
For the food delivery firm, employee benefit expenses emerged as Swish’s largest cost component, accounting for 38.47% of its total expenditure. The company spent Rs 55.7 crore on this head in FY26, against Rs 10.4 crore in FY25, marking a 5.4X increase. Of this, Rs 17.5 crore went towards delivery partner expenses, while the remaining costs covered its workforce.
The cost of materials, which primarily includes ingredients and other inputs required for food preparation, surged 6.9X to Rs 39.5 crore from Rs 5.75 crore in FY25. It accounted for 27.28% of the company's overall expenses.
Marketing and branding emerged as another significant cost head, which rose 9.4X to Rs 19 crore from Rs 2.03 crore in the previous fiscal year. The expense accounted for 13.12% of the total expenditure.
Among other expenses, rent stood at Rs 6.16 crore, while registration, renewals and subscription costs amounted to Rs 4.64 crore. Kitchen operations, housekeeping, professional charges, logistics and other overheads contributed to the overall expense base of Rs 144.8 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 23.2 crore in FY25.
Amid a sharp rise in employee costs, marketing spends and other operational expenses, Swish’s losses surged 4.8X to Rs 91 crore in FY26 from Rs 19 crore in the previous fiscal year.
Its EBITDA margin and Return on Capital Employed (ROCE) stood at -193.2% and -30.9%, respectively.

On a unit level, the Accel-backed startup spent Rs 3.04 to earn every rupee of operating revenue in FY26. As of March 2026, it had total current assets of Rs 43 crore, including cash and bank balances of Rs 28 crore.
Swish has raised around $78 million to date, including a recent $24 million round led by Bertelsmann India Investments, with participation from existing investors Accel, Bain Capital Ventures and Hara Global, as exclusively reported by Entrackr. Earlier in March, it raised $38 million in a round led by Hara Global and Bain Capital Ventures.
Backed by fresh funding, Swish is strengthening its kitchen infrastructure and delivery network, while looking to expand into other parts of the country. This is expected to support revenue growth in the coming years, although improving kitchen utilisation, managing delivery costs and building repeat demand will be key to narrowing its losses.

The board of the Mumbai-based has passed a special resolution to issue  18,090 compulsory convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 21,221.92 per share to raise the aforesaid amount, according to the documents reviewed by Entrackr.
Prosus, through its investment arm MIH Investments One B.V., will lead the round with an investment of Rs 28.80 crore. Elevation Capital and Vertex Ventures will also participate, investing Rs 6.04 crore and Rs 2.30 crore, respectively. Eximius Ventures will invest the remaining Rs 1.25 crore.

Founded in 2022 by Gaurav Mittal, Himanshu Agrawal, Puneet Sharma and Abhinav Garg, Vegapay is building a technology stack for digital lending and card management. Its platform enables banks, NBFCs and other financial institutions to launch and manage customised credit products, including credit, debit and prepaid cards, credit lines on UPI, loan origination and collection systems. 
In August 2026, Moneycontrol reported that Vegapay was in talks to raise $15-20 million from Prosus and others.

title: Cosine Robots raises Rs 22.36 Cr led by Avaana Capital
summary:
Bengaluru-based deeptech startup Cosine Robots has raised Rs 22.36 crore ($2.4 million) in a funding round led by Avaana Capital, with participation from WEH Ventures and angel investors.
The proceeds will be used to set up a dedicated research and development (R&D) and production facility, expand its engineering team and accelerate the development of its integrated servo actuator portfolio.
Founded by Kiran Mathew Koshy and Delip Thomas, Cosine Robots develops actuators and motion systems for robotics applications. Its products combine motors, gearboxes, sensors, electronics and proprietary control software into integrated systems designed to control robotic movement.
The company is developing a common motion architecture through a modular range of cycloidal and planetary actuators. These products are designed for different torque requirements across industrial robotic arms, collaborative robots, quadrupeds and humanoid robots.
Cosine’s technology also includes a proprietary control architecture that combines dual-position sensing with a 25 kHz control loop, enabling 25,000 updates per second. The system is designed to improve precision and control over movement and torque.

title: AppsForBharat’s revenue jumps 84% to Rs 129 Cr in FY26
summary:
AppsForBharat, the company behind devotional platform Sri Mandir, reported strong growth in FY26, with its operating revenue surging 84.3% year-on-year to Rs 129 crore from Rs 70 crore in FY25.
The Bengaluru-based startup’s revenue rose 84.3% to Rs 129 crore in FY26 from Rs 70 crore in FY25, as per its financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).


Sri Mandir offers online puja services for devotees unable to visit temples. Priests perform rituals in devotees’ names and gotras, with videos shared afterwards. Sri Mandir launched these services in 2022 with four to five temples and now partners with over 100 temples across India.
AppsForBharat is consolidating operations in temple towns such as Ujjain, Haridwar and Mathura, while expanding its presence in South India.
The company generated Rs 125.62 crore from the sale of services, contributing around 97% of its operating revenue. The remaining Rs 3.3 crore came from the sale of products, accounting for approximately 3% of total revenue.
Including other income, AppsForBharat's total income increased to Rs 141 crore in FY26 from Rs 73 crore in the previous fiscal year.
On the expense front, advertising and promotional expenses remained the largest cost component, rising to Rs 98.5 crore in FY26 from Rs 52 crore in FY25. Employee benefit expenses increased 78.1% to Rs 57 crore from Rs 32 crore.
Puja and chadhava expenses nearly doubled to Rs 22 crore in FY26 from Rs 11.4 crore in FY25. Meanwhile, tools and technology expenses increased 23.5% to Rs 12.6 crore from Rs 10.2 crore, while other expenses rose 45.2% to Rs 18 crore.
Overall, the company's total expenses increased 76.3% to Rs 208 crore in FY26 from Rs 118 crore in FY25.
Despite revenue growing faster than expenses, the company's net loss widened 49.8% to Rs 67.8 crore in FY26 from Rs 45.26 crore in the previous fiscal year. Meanwhile, its EBITDA margin improved to -61.05% from -67.76% in FY25, while ROCE stood at -32.64% during the fiscal year.


At a unit level, AppsForBharat spent Rs 1.61 to earn a rupee of operating revenue in FY26, compared with Rs 1.69 in the previous fiscal year. Its cash and bank balance declined to Rs 9 crore from Rs 38.5 crore, while current assets stood at Rs 200 crore as of March 2026, against Rs 164 crore a year earlier.
Prashant Sachan, Founder and CEO, said the company continues to invest in its team, AI and initiatives related to temples and priests.
“When we started in 2020, the question was whether families would trust technology with something as personal as their prayers. Six years on, the numbers have answered that, and more devotees than ever can take part in rituals at the temples they hold dear, wherever they are. Our focus now is to strengthen that trust on the ground, by building our presence in temple towns and working with more temples,” said Sachan.
The company raised Rs 175 crore ($20 million) in a Series C round led by Susquehanna Asia Venture Capital in July 2025. It has raised more than $50 million to date and is also backed by Fundamentum, Elevation Capital and Peak XV Partners.

title: Pee Safe’s revenue jumps 54% to Rs 126 Cr in FY26, posts Rs 7 Cr loss
summary:
Personal hygiene and wellness brand Pee Safe reported a 54% year-on-year growth in its operating revenue in FY26. However, the company continued to remain in the red during the fiscal year.
Pee Safe’s revenue from operations rose 53.7% to Rs 126 crore in FY26 from Rs 82 crore in FY25, as per its financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Founded by Vikas Bagaria and Srijana Bagaria, Pee Safe offers a range of personal hygiene and wellness products across categories such as menstrual care, intimate hygiene, toilet hygiene, sexual wellness, and grooming. Its product portfolio includes sanitary pads, menstrual cups, tampons, intimate washes, toilet seat sanitizers, lubricants and grooming products.
Revenue from product sales remained the company's sole source of operating revenue, while it generated an additional Rs 1 crore through other income, taking its total income to Rs 127 crore in FY26.
Advertising and promotional expenses, the largest cost component, surged 76.3% to Rs 46 crore in FY26 from Rs 26.09 crore in FY25, accounting for around 34% of total expenses. Cost of materials consumed, another major expense head, increased 59.3% to Rs 43 crore. Employee benefit expenses rose 37.9% to Rs 17.58 crore, while freight costs grew 43.6% to Rs 7.18 crore. Other expenses also increased 29.2% to Rs 20.24 crore.
Overall, Pee Safe’s total expenses increased 54.9% to Rs 134 crore in FY26 from Rs 86.5 crore in FY25.
As expenses grew slightly faster than revenue, Pee Safe's losses jumped 80% to Rs 7.2 crore in FY26 from Rs 4 crore in FY25. Its ROCE stood at -15.36%, while its EBITDA margin was -5.72% during FY26.

On a unit level, the company spent Rs 1.06 to earn a rupee of operating revenue in FY26. Pee Safe’s current assets stood at Rs 77.7 crore, Cash and bank balances jumped 16.8X to Rs 39 crore in FY26 from Rs 2.32 crore in FY25
The Gurugram-based firm has raised around $45 million in funding to date, including a $32 million funding round led by OrbiMed, a global healthcare-focused private equity firm.

The funding round values the company at around Rs 191.5 crore on a post-money basis. 
The fresh capital towards accelerating digital growth, strengthening brand building and expanding into physical retail, Zavya said in a press release.
Co-founded in 2021 by Poem Kabra and Ravi Malani, Zavya focuses on everyday 925 sterling silver jewellery, combining contemporary designs with a digital-first distribution strategy. The company said it has achieved EBITDA profitability while scaling its business through a capital-efficient approach.
The latest investment also marks the entry of Daksham Growth Ventures, while Orios Venture Partners has continued to back the company.
Zavya plans to strengthen its presence across direct-to-consumer (D2C) and quick commerce channels, invest in brand building and make its initial foray into physical retail, according to the company.
The funding comes amid changing jewellery consumption patterns in India, with rising gold prices and evolving consumer preferences driving interest in alternative precious metals. Younger consumers are increasingly exploring hallmarked 925 sterling silver jewellery as a more accessible option for everyday wear, combining precious-metal value with contemporary designs.
While silver jewellery has an established presence in international markets, the category remains relatively underpenetrated in India, particularly across organised and online retail channels, presenting an opportunity for design-led brands.
Zavya sells through its own website and mobile application, quick-commerce platforms such as Blinkit and Zepto, and marketplaces including Amazon, Myntra and Nykaa, where it claims to be among the top brands in its category.
The brand launches more than 50 new jewellery styles every month through weekly product drops. It also reported eight-figure net sales in a single day during Rakshabandhan, highlighting demand during gifting occasions.

summary:
Ionic Wealth, the wealth-tech platform backed by Angel One, has raised Rs 177 crore in a strategic funding round led by Angel One and marquee families.
The latest fundraise takes the company’s cumulative capital raised to around Rs 466 crore.
The capital will be used to strengthen its portfolio-led proposition, integrate artificial intelligence (AI) into its platform, expand its ultra-high-net-worth individual (UHNI) business, hire specialised talent and increase its presence in India and overseas markets, Ionic Wealth said in a press release.
The Mumbai-based firm has crossed Rs 16,000 crore in assets under management (AUM), with a combined high-net-worth individual (HNI) and UHNI client base of over 2,900 across more than 12 cities. It has a team of over 100 private bankers and achieved these milestones within two years of operations.
Co-founded by Srikanth Subramanian, Shobhit Mathur and Dharmendra Jain in 2024, Ionic Wealth began operations with an initial investment of around Rs 290 crore from Angel One and marquee families.
The company has scaled its AUM more than fourfold, from around Rs 3,800 crore in March 2025 to over Rs 16,000 crore in September 2026. Its client base also nearly quadrupled during the same period, from around 680 to over 2,900.
All investors from the previous round participated in the latest funding round. These include business families, Bollywood personalities, fintech entrepreneurs, global CXOs, board advisors and media houses, among others.
Ionic Wealth plans to use the fresh capital to scale its HNI business through technology, strengthen global investing capabilities through GIFT City and broaden investment access through the Accredited Investor framework and Specialised Investment Funds (SIFs). It also plans to build a dedicated UHNI proposition for India’s leading families.
Ionic Wealth operates an omnichannel wealth-tech platform focused on HNIs and UHNIs, offering investment opportunities across asset classes, digital wealth management services and customised investment roadmaps. Its asset-management business operates across portfolio management services (PMS), investment advisory and alternative investment funds (AIFs). Its GIFT City business is registered with the International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA).

summary:
Fintech startup InPrime Finserv has  recently raised Rs 101.20 crore in its Series B funding round, led by new investor FMO, with participation from existing investor Z47 (formerly Matrix Partners), Pravega Ventures and other individual investors.
The company had previously raised Rs 50 crore in its Series A1 round, led by Pravega Ventures, along with participation from existing investors Z47, InfoEdge Ventures and Kettleborough VC.
To take a closer look at the Bengaluru-based firm’s latest Series B round, Entrackr reviewed its regulatory filings to break down the round details, updated cap table and valuation uplift.
According to RoC filings accessed by Entrackr, the company allotted 10 equity shares and 7,40,040 CCPS at Rs 1,029.50 apiece, along with another 2,40,995 CCPS at Rs 1,037.37 apiece, to raise a combined Rs 101 crore.
The Netherlands-based development finance institution FMO led the round with an investment of Rs 60 crore, followed by Z47 (Formerly Matrix Partners) with Rs 25 crore and Pravega Ventures with Rs 15 crore.
Among other investors, Sreekanth Nagarajan invested Rs 50 lakh, followed by Pushpendra Kumar Singh, Vishwajeet Kumar and Sourabh Maheshwari invested Rs 10 lakh each. The company also raised Rs 21 lakh from several other individual investors.
Separately, the firm also issued 1,000 non-convertible debentures (NCDs) at a face value of Rs 1 lakh each to raise Rs 10 crore from Ambium Finserve Limited and Mufin Green Finance Limited.
As per Entrackr's estimates, InPrime Finserv's post-money valuation jumped 2X to Rs 360 crore in its Series B round from Rs 180 crore in Series A. 
The fresh capital will be used to expand the company's lending operations, strengthen its artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities across underwriting and customer service, and diversify into micro-mortgage products, InPrime Finserv said in a press release.
Founded in 2021 by Sneh Thakur, Manish Raj and Rajat Singh, InPrime Finserv focuses on providing credit to underserved informal prime households, including micro and nano entrepreneurs, self-employed professionals, small retailers and individuals engaged in farming and allied agricultural activities.
After the allotment of Series B, Z47 (Formerly Matrix Partners) remains the largest external shareholder with a 21.39% stake, followed by FMO with 16.66%, Pravega Ventures with 15% and Info Edge Ventures with 10.43%. Meanwhile co-founders, Rajat Kumar Singh, Manish Kumar Raj and Sneh Thakur hold 12.76%, 9.50% and 6.24% stakes, respectively.

title: EloElo Group launches Dolphin AI Film Studio at IFFI 2026
summary:
EloElo Group, the parent company of Story TV, has launched an AI-powered film production platform, Dolphin AI Film Studio, at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa.
The platform is designed for filmmakers, studios, production houses and independent creators. It brings multiple stages of video production, from script development to finished content, onto a single platform.
The launch took place in the presence of Chanchal Kumar, Secretary, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.
Dolphin AI Film Studio aims to reduce production costs and time while enabling creators to produce short-form and long-form video content. It also includes World Lock technology to maintain visual consistency across characters, locations and props throughout a production.
The platform will initially support micro-dramas. Other formats, including short films, web series, feature films, animated content, documentaries, advertisements and music videos, are planned for future releases.
Saurabh Pandey, founder and CEO of EloElo Group, said the platform aims to address production constraints related to cost, time and scale by bringing AI tools and production capabilities into a single environment.

title: Funding and acquisitions in Indian startups this week [Nov 16- Nov 21]
summary:
This week, 23 Indian startups raised $290 million across 6 growth-stage and 17 early-stage deals, including two undisclosed rounds. The week also saw five key appointments, two exits and one fund launch.
In contrast, 12 startups had collectively secured about $31.3 million in the previous week.
[Growth-stage deals]
Growth-stage startups raised $290 million across six deals this week. AI-native CRM startup Dreamteam raised $53 million in a funding round with participation from Together Fund, Accel and Premji Invest, Nexon Omniverse, the parent company of value fashion retailer Style Union, has raised Rs 485 crore (approximately $52 million) in a Series E funding round. Bubble tea and Korean street food brand Boba Bhai raised $18 million. 
Robotics company Botsync raised $11 million in a Series B funding round led by IvyCap Ventures and Bengaluru-based InPrime Finserv has raised Rs 101 crore (approximately $10.7 million) in a Series B funding round led by FMO, among others. 
[Early-stage deals]
Early-stage startups raised $147.7 million across 17 deals this week. Bengaluru-based Humyn Labs raised $47 million in a Series A round comprising equity and debt. The round includes $26 million in equity and $21 million in venture debt. Semiconductor startup Bharat Semi raised $24 million in a seed funding round led by Info Edge Group, South Park Commons and Indus Bridge Ventures.
Branded egg company Henfruit raised $15 million in a Series A funding round led by Lok Capital. Coimbatore-based sweets and snacks chain Shree Anandhaas raised Rs 110 crore in a fresh funding round led by new investor Ayra Ventures.
Fatehpuria Hygiene, a trade, supply chain and fulfilment company, raised Rs 100 crore in its maiden equity funding round led by investor Madhu Kela.
[City and segment-wise deals]
Bengaluru led startup funding activity with 12 deals during the week, followed by Mumbai and Delhi-NCR with three deals each. Coimbatore, Rajasthan, Pune and Thiruvananthapuram also recorded funding this week.
AI startups led sector-wise funding activity with six deals, followed by e-commerce, semiconductor, FMCG, robotics. Startups across fintech, legal tech, healthtech also raised funds during the week.
[Series-wise deals]
Seed rounds led funding activity with five deals, followed by four Series B rounds. Series E, Series A, maiden, debt, pre-Series A and angel also saw activity during the week.
[Week-on-week funding trend]
On a weekly basis, startup funding increased nearly 826% to $290 million from $31.3 million raised in the previous week.
The average weekly funding over the past eight weeks stood at around $206.9 million across 23 deals.
[Key Hirings]
CarDekho Group appointed Sudhir Pai as CEO of its auto classifieds business and group strategy head.
Medi Assist Healthcare Services appointed Aruna Vaidyanathan, formerly Global Head of Growth Marketing at TCS.
Indian deep-tech company Naxatra Labs has appointed Naveen Deepak Veeramaneni as its Chief Product Officer.
[Departures]
Kriti Gupta, vice president at Peak XV Partners, has quit the venture capital firm after five years to join Goodwater Capital.
PB Fintech co-founder Alok Bansal will step down as Executive Vice Chairman and Whole Time Director on March 31, 2027. He will continue on the company's board as a Non-Executive, Non-Independent Director from April 1, 2027.
[Fund Launches]
Oister Global, an India-focused private markets asset manager, has launched a growth-stage deep tech fund with a target corpus of Rs 400 crore and a greenshoe option of Rs 200 crore, taking its potential size to Rs 600 crore.
[News flash this week]
▪️ Fractal Analytics explores acquisitions of up to 25 AI startups
Fractal Analytics is in discussions with 20–25 AI startups as it looks to expand its capabilities across healthcare, agentic AI and AI engineering. The company is open to acquisitions worth up to Rs 1,000 crore, with a preferred deal size of $50 million to $100 million.
▪️ OpenAI appoints Pragya Misra to lead business development in India and South Asia
OpenAI's India head of strategy and global affairs, Pragya Misra, is moving into a new role to lead business development across India and South Asia. She joined OpenAI in 2024 as its first employee in India.
▪️ CarDekho Group appoints former Magicbricks CEO Sudhir Pai
CarDekho Group has appointed Sudhir Pai as CEO of its auto classifieds business and Group Strategy Head. He will oversee platforms including CarDekho.com, ZigWheels and BikeDekho.
▪️ PhonePe partners with Kerala Startup Mission to support startups
PhonePe has partnered with Kerala Startup Mission to support startups through digital payment infrastructure, onboarding assistance and technical support. The partnership will also include workshops and knowledge-sharing initiatives.
▪️ Drip Capital signs Rs 5,000 Cr trade finance pact with Bihar government
Drip Capital has signed an MoU with Bihar's Department of Industries to facilitate up to Rs 5,000 crore in trade finance for MSME exporters over five years. The partnership will provide collateral-free working capital and connect local manufacturers with domestic and international buyers.
▪️ Rediff files updated draft papers for Rs 600 Cr IPO
Rediff.com India has filed updated draft IPO papers proposing a fresh issue of equity shares worth Rs 600 crore, without an offer-for-sale component. The company operates consumer internet and enterprise communication businesses.

title: Rooter’s revenue jumps over 2X to Rs 170 Cr in FY26; losses shrink 40%
summary:
India’s gaming industry is moving beyond gameplay, with live streaming, esports, gaming communities and in-game commerce creating new opportunities for platforms. Companies such as Rooter are looking to capitalise on this growing market by bringing gamers, content creators and publishers onto a single platform. Rising mobile gaming adoption and new monetisation avenues have further increased interest in the segment.
Founded in 2016 by Piyush Kumar and Dipesh Agarwal, Rooter operates a gaming live-streaming and commerce platform that allows users to stream and watch gameplay across popular titles such as BGMI, Call of Duty and Valorant, while engaging with gaming creators. The company has also entered gaming commerce, selling in-game currencies and gift cards to build a revenue stream beyond advertising and content.
Rooter’s strategy appears to be gaining traction, with the company more than doubling its operating revenue to Rs 170.4 crore in FY26 from Rs 78.9 crore in the previous financial year, while narrowing its losses by 40% to Rs 19.2 crore, according to its financial statements reviewed by Entrackr.


Rooter also operates a gaming commerce business that sells in-game currencies, vouchers and digital gift cards alongside its live-streaming and virtual gifting offerings. However, the company has not disclosed a segment-wise revenue breakdown in its financial statements.
Rooter’s total expenses increased 69.5% to Rs 189.7 crore in FY26 from Rs 111.9 crore in FY25. The largest expense component was the cost of materials, which surged 3.4X to Rs 146.7 crore, and accounted for around 77% of the total expenditure. The expense likely comprises purchases of in-game currencies, vouchers and digital gift cards sourced from publishers and distributors for resale through Rooter Shop.
On the other hand, employee benefit expenses declined 21% to Rs 14.6 crore in FY26. Miscellaneous and other expenses, which include IT, legal and professional fees, rent and other overheads, collectively stood at around Rs 28 crore in FY26
Consequently, Rooter narrowed its losses by 40% to Rs 19.2 crore in FY26 from Rs 32 crore in FY25, despite higher commerce-related expenses. Its EBITDA margin stood at -9.97% during the year.
On a unit level, Rooter spent Rs 1.11 to generate every rupee of operating revenue during the last fiscal year As of March 2026, the company had current assets worth Rs 50.3 crore.
The growth comes amid an expanding gaming ecosystem in India. According to a report by Niko Partners, India's gaming market generated $1.04 billion in revenue in 2025, registering 14.8% year-on-year growth. The number of gamers stood at an estimated 511 million during the year. 
Rooter claims to have built a community of over 85 million registered users and raised around $40 million from investors, including Lightbox Ventures, Duane Park Ventures and March Gaming, as it looks to strengthen its position in gaming streaming and commerce.
The firm certainly seems to have the momentum behind it to cross over into break-even territory or perhaps even a decent profit next year, but will face the challenge of remaining on its toes throughout. The category remains fickle and prone to trend watching, mimicking the profile of users in some ways. Rooter has the experience behind it to ride the right trend when it shifts, and we believe the firm is well poised to to deliver soon.

title: InPrime Finserv raises Rs 101 Cr in Series B round led by FMO
summary:
Bengaluru-based InPrime Finserv has raised Rs 101 crore (approximately $10.7 million) in a Series B funding round led by FMO, the Dutch entrepreneurial development bank. Existing investors Z47 (formerly Matrix Partners India) and Pravega Ventures also participated in the round.
The fresh capital will be used to expand the company's lending operations, strengthen its artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities across underwriting and customer service, and diversify into micro-mortgage products, InPrime Finserv said in a press release.
The company also plans to deepen investments in agentic AI and AI co-pilots to improve credit assessment and customer engagement.
Founded by Sneh Thakur, Manish Raj and Rajat Singh in 2021, InPrime began operations in 2023. The company is an AI-first non-banking financial company (NBFC) focused on India's emerging middle class, particularly customers operating in the informal economy, including kirana store owners, dairy farmers, beauty parlour owners, small retailers and micro-entrepreneurs.
InPrime uses AI-driven underwriting, data analytics and an on-ground presence to serve customers who often struggle to access formal credit despite owning property and running established businesses.
The company's AI capabilities are already deployed in its operations. Four in-house AI co-pilots support its credit team, while three agentic AI voice agents handled more than 126,000 customer calls between April and September 2026.
Currently, InPrime operates 46 area offices across Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Haryana, Uttarakhand and Madhya Pradesh. It has served more than 27,000 households and disbursed Rs 516.92 crore in loans to date.
As of September 30, 2026, the company's assets under management (AUM) stood at Rs 332.8 crore, while its gross non-performing assets (GNPA) were at 0.80%. With the latest fundraise, InPrime's total funding has reached Rs 190 crore.
InPrime's existing investors also include Info Edge Ventures, Kettleborough VC and Titan Capital.

title: Paytm, Pine Labs, MobiKwik shares tank over 7% amid reports of further UPI MDR delay
summary:
Shares of digital payments companies Paytm, Pine Labs and Mobikwik came under sharp selling pressure on Thursday after reports suggested that the proposed merchant discount rate (MDR) on select Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions could face another delay, potentially extending beyond the 2027 assembly elections.
As of 3:00 PM (today), One 97 Communications, the parent company of Paytm, was trading at Rs 1,741.6, down around 7.85% from its previous close of Rs 1,890. Pine Labs was trading at Rs 161.5, down 4.6%, while MobiKwik was at around Rs 209.9, declining 7.42% from its previous close of Rs 226.72.
The proposed MDR framework was expected to provide an additional revenue stream for payment companies by allowing charges on select high-value merchant UPI transactions. However, according to media reports, the rollout could be pushed beyond the assembly elections scheduled across five states in the first half of 2027, as the government remains cautious about potential opposition from merchants and trade associations.
The rollout was initially scheduled for October 15, 2026, but was deferred until after Diwali following resistance from retailers. The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the government are yet to arrive at a consensus on a fresh implementation date.
The development comes at a time when Paytm had been witnessing a recovery in its share price, supported by improving financial performance and regulatory developments. The stock had traded at Rs 1,939.70 on November 13, around 9.8% below its IPO price of Rs 2,150.
The sell-off comes despite all three companies reporting improved financial performance in Q2 FY27. Paytm has remained profitable for six consecutive quarters. Its operating revenue grew 28.5% year-on-year to Rs 2,648 crore, while net profit jumped 10.7 times to Rs 225 crore.
Pine Labs reported a 24% year-on-year increase in operating revenue to Rs 806 crore in Q2 FY27. Its net profit surged 6.5 times to Rs 39 crore from Rs 6 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
MobiKwik also posted its highest-ever quarterly profit after tax of Rs 11.8 crore in Q2 FY27, compared to a loss of Rs 28.6 crore in the year-ago period. Its operating revenue grew over 9% to Rs 295.7 crore.

summary:
AI governance and assurance startup Disseqt AI has raised $8 million in pre-Series A funding round led by Gresham House Ventures, with participation from existing investor Sure Valley Ventures (SVV), Delta Partners and Enterprise Ireland.
The round also saw participation from angel investors, including senior executives from OpenAI, Palo Alto Networks, Salesforce and Meta, along with former Indian cricket captain Rahul Dravid, who invested in his individual capacity.
The fresh funds will be utilized to expand its enterprise customer base globally and  hiring across sales, operations and technology roles in India, Disseqt said in a press release.
Founded in late 2025 by Apoorva Kumar, Manish Atri and Cyril Treacy, Disseqt AI provides an AI governance and assurance platform that helps enterprises test, monitor and govern AI applications and agents.
Its platform enables businesses to assess AI agents for vulnerabilities before deployment, enforce company policies once they go live, and continuously monitor their behaviour. It can also block outputs that violate organisational policies while maintaining audit trails for compliance and oversight.
The platform allows enterprises to test whether AI agents can be manipulated into revealing confidential customer information or exhibiting other vulnerabilities before being deployed in business operations.
The funding comes amid growing enterprise adoption of AI agents and increasing concerns around their safety, security and regulatory compliance. According to McKinsey's 2026 State of AI survey, 40% of respondents at companies with annual revenues exceeding $1 billion were scaling AI agents in at least one business function, compared with 27% a year earlier.
Disseqt said it has already deployed its assurance capabilities across multiple enterprise use cases. In a project involving a global sports league's fan engagement agent, which serves 80 million fans, the company improved the safe-response rate from 80% to 99% across tests covering safety, bias and privacy risks. It added that no unsafe outputs were detected when the original failing tests were repeated after fixes.
The company also provides assurance services for a credit card services programme at a large European bank.
The investment marks another bet on the emerging AI governance and assurance segment, as enterprises look to deploy autonomous AI systems across customer interactions, financial services and internal business operations.

title: Dialysis care provider VitusCare raises $3 Mn in Series B round
summary:
Dialysis care provider VitusCare has raised $3 million in a Series B funding round with participation from Singapore-based healthcare growth equity firm Liberty Ridge Capital, HDFC Bank, Equentis, NAFA Capital Advisors, existing investors 1Crowd and 3i Partners, along with several angel investors.
The Gurugram-based company had previously raised $2.7 million in a Series A round led by Tomorrow Capital in April 2024 and Rs 10.83 crore in a seed round in 2019.
The fresh capital will be deployed towards expanding its dialysis centre network, technology development, workforce training and international expansion, VitusCare said in a press release.
The fundraise comes as VitusCare has nearly tripled its revenue since its previous funding round in 2024. The company has expanded its network from 22 to more than 60 dialysis centres across nine states and over 50 cities.
So far, VitusCare has treated more than 35,000 patients and conducted over 8 lakh dialysis sessions. Its workforce has also grown from 110 to 300 employees.
The company said it reported positive corporate EBITDA in FY26, supported by faster breakeven at newly opened centres and same-centre growth of over 30%.
Founded in 2017 by Prabhat Shrivastava, VitusCare operates through a capital-light ‘shop-in-shop’ model. It partners with existing hospitals to provide specialised dialysis services instead of setting up standalone facilities.
The company aims to expand its network to more than 100 centres by the end of FY27. It is also exploring opportunities in select Asian markets.
VitusCare is also developing AI-native business modules to improve healthcare delivery and plans to establish a Technician Academy to train dialysis professionals.
The company competes with players such as NephroPlus, Apex Kidney Care, DCDC Kidney Care, 7Med and Rahi Care.
Under the shop-in-shop model, dialysis providers supply equipment, trained medical professionals, technology and operational support while using hospitals’ existing infrastructure. This allows them to expand their reach with lower capital expenditure, particularly in Tier II and III cities.
Other players in the segment include DCDC Kidney Care, which raised Rs 150 crore from Temasek-backed ABC Impact in March 2025, and The Renal Project, which secured $1.3 million in a pre-seed round led by JITO Angel Network in September 2026.
